alt: Time bars per input from 0 to 150 s. Original checker: about 30 s of computing, then the 60 s limit, and the promised range from 60 to 150 s marked as timed out. Fixed checker: a full 150 s bar, at most 4 inputs at once with one CPU each. A table shows three test submissions (13 s per case, 80 s and 140 s of computing per input): all 50 inputs time out with no score on the original checker, all 50 scored on the fixed one. A box notes the documented, unfixed ceiling of about 30.6 out of 100 (30.3 before rounding).
caption: Warehouse Forklift Routing solutions that use the time the instructions promise get no score. The instructions promise 30 s per test case, or 150 s per five-case input, but the original checker stops each input at 60 s. On EdgeBench's 4-CPU setting it also runs 8 inputs at once, so each gets only about 30 s of computing, and one timeout leaves the whole submission without a score. Test submissions that wait 13 s per case or compute 80 or 140 s per input got no score under the original checker. Under the fixed one, which allows 150 s and runs no more inputs at once than it has CPUs, all 50 inputs were scored. (The fix also needs a longer final wait in EdgeBench's runner, which is tested only in parts.) A separate limit is documented, not fixed: no valid answer can score above about 30.6 out of 100.
